verdict: Fastenal grew sales 16% to $2.5B by winning bigger customers, and keeping overhead growth well below sales growth turned that into a 20% jump in profit.

segments.name: Manufacturing customers
segments.note: Factories — heavy and other manufacturing took 76.6% of sales, growing fastest.

segments.name: Other end markets
segments.note: Resellers, government, education, transport, warehouses and data centers — 15.4% of sales.

segments.name: Non-residential construction
segments.note: Building sites — 8.0% of sales, growing for a sixth straight quarter.

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Staff, stores, trucks and running the company — grew 9%, well below sales growth of 16%.

otherDetail: Net interest income of $0.4M — interest earned roughly matched interest paid on Fastenal's small debt balance.

takeaways.title: Big customers are driving growth
takeaways.text: Daily sales rose 15.5%. Contract customers — large accounts with signed deals — grew 18.8% and are now 76.5% of sales, as Fastenal keeps winning share inside factories.

takeaways.title: Overhead leverage beat margin pressure
takeaways.text: Gross margin slipped to 44.8% because big customers get lower prices, but SG&A fell to 23.3% of sales from 24.6%, so operating margin rose to 21.5% — and operating income jumped 20%, the biggest dollar gain in Fastenal's history.

takeaways.title: Most profit went back to shareholders
takeaways.text: Fastenal returned $328M — 82% of net income — as $298M of dividends and $30M of share buybacks, while keeping total debt at just $100M.

footerNote: Fastenal reports one segment, so revenue is split by end market using the release's percentage-of-sales table (manufacturing 76.6%, other 15.4%, non-residential construction 8.0%). Fastenal reports in tenths of a million; figures here are rounded to the nearest $M (net sales $2,463.3M, gross profit $1,104.7M, SG&A $573.9M, operating income $530.8M, tax $129.6M, net income $401.6M).
